title: Interaction-Breaking Adversarial Learning Framework for Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
claim: Coordinated group behavior can be broken by perturbing agents' observations or actions, which disrupts cooperation.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared bottom legend, red X marks on game screenshots
description: Three side-by-side StarCraft II game screenshots labeled (a) Normal, (b) Observation Attack and (c) Action Attack. Each shows two groups of Protoss units: G1 with orange outlines and G2 with blue outlines. They face a large Zerg enemy and a smaller green-glowing one. In (a), both groups fire light-blue beams at the same large enemy. A translucent orange circle marks G1's sight range. In (b), red crosses over G2's eyes mark masked observations, and G1's beams split toward the smaller enemy. In (c), a red arrow shows G1's perturbed movement, and red crosses cut some of G1's beams. A bottom legend maps orange to Group 1, blue to Group 2, red to Attack, and the circle icon to G1 sight range. The eye goes first to the beams and red marks.
caption: Illustration of the proposed interaction-breaking attack in StarCraft II. (a) Normal setting, where agents in $G_1$ and $G_2$ coordinate their attack on the same enemy. (b) Observation attack, where red crosses indicate masked observation components. (c) Action attack, where the red arrow denotes the perturbed action.
abstract: Cooperation is central to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), yet learned coordination can be fragile when external perturbations disrupt inter-agent interactions. Prior robust MARL methods have primarily considered value-oriented attacks, leaving a gap in robustness when interaction structures themselves are corrupted. In this paper, we propose an interaction-breaking adversarial learning (IBAL) framework that takes an information-theoretic view to construct attacks that impede coordination by perturbing agents' observations and actions, and trains agents to perform reliably under such disruptions. Empirically, our approach improves robustness over existing robust MARL baselines across diverse attack settings and yields stronger performance even under agent-missing scenarios. Our code is available at https://sunwoolee0504.github.io/IBAL.
